summary: Cut fresh database initialisation cost (#136) (#151)
details: * perf(db): cut fresh database initialisation cost (#136) A fresh test database spent ~1.25 s in `initializeDatabase`, called 18 times per suite (~22 s). Index creation dominated: 92 `createIndex` calls, each a journal commit on a newly created collection. - Group the index catalogue by collection and send one `createIndexes` command per collection (46 commands). Keys, names, uniqueness, partial filters, TTL and `expireAfterSeconds` are unchanged; a failed grouped command falls back to per-index creation so one legacy conflict cannot block the rest, as before. - Bulk-write the 78 baseline policies instead of one upsert per record. - Split startup into `ensureDatabaseIndexes` (new `src/lib/db-indexes.ts`) and `seedBaselineContent`. `initializeDatabase` still runs both, so production startup and `getDatabase` are unchanged. Mongo tests that seed their own content use the schema half; notification-outbox keeps the full path and asserts the seeded register and indexes. - The in-memory preview implements `createIndexes` and `bulkWrite`. Verified on the local replica set: index phase 1.44 s -> 0.76 s and total 1.27 s -> 0.95 s over six interleaved pairs (shared host, so absolute wall time varied). A fresh database has the same 47 collections and 139 indexes, and the same 78 proposals and revisions, before and after. Full suite (833 tests) passed twice; each run left only `admin`, `config`, `engage` and `local`. * chore(changelog): record database initialisation change (#136) * fix(settings): tie-break site settings events by insertion order * chore(changelog): record the site event ordering fix

summary: Bound comment vote retries by time, not attempt count (#123) (#134)
details: * fix(discussion): bound comment vote retries by time with backoff (#123) The comment vote compare-and-swap gave up after 12 fixed attempts with a 2-8 ms jitter. On a cold replica set the first write can take hundreds of milliseconds, so 25 concurrent voters exhausted the attempts and valid votes failed with 'Comment votes changed at the same time. Try again.' Retry on a five-second time budget instead, with exponential backoff and jitter (4 ms doubling to a 250 ms cap). Legitimate contention converges even when writes are slow; a genuinely stuck writer still fails in bounded time. Exactly-once is unchanged. The write is still one version-filtered compare-and-swap of the whole vote state, so a lost race writes nothing and retries against the committed state. Voter arrays, switching between upvotes and downvotes, and the persisted shape are untouched. Expiry now logs comment_vote_retry_budget_exhausted with the comment ID, attempt count and budget only - never member IDs or vote choices - before throwing. Tests add a deterministic cold-write case (40 ms per comment write) that fails under the old attempt count and passes now, plus a stuck-writer case proving the budget is bounded and the warning is emitted without identities. * chore(changelog): record bounded comment vote retries (#123) Regenerates the public snapshot so the fix commit appears on /changelog/. The 80-commit window still drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96. * fix(discussion): make the comment vote retry budget configurable (#123) The 5 s retry budget was a fixed constant. Under full-suite load the injected 40 ms cold-write test needed longer than 5 s to converge and failed, even though votes were not actually lost. Read the budget from ENGAGE_COMMENT_VOTE_RETRY_BUDGET_MS at call time. Unset, empty or invalid values use the 5000 ms default; values are clamped to 250-60000 ms so a bad setting cannot remove the bound. The expiry warning records the effective budget. The stress test now runs with a 15000 ms budget, proving convergence under injected slow writes on a loaded machine while production keeps the 5 s default. The stuck-writer test uses the 250 ms floor so it stays fast, and asserts the default, fallback and clamp rules. Exactly-once is unchanged: the write is still one version-filtered compare-and-swap of the whole vote state, and no persisted shape or privacy boundary changed. * chore(changelog): record the configurable comment vote retry budget (#123) Regenerates the public snapshot so the stabilisation commit appears on /changelog/. * refactor(discussion): inject the comment vote retry budget instead of an environment variable (#123) Configuration belongs in the administration panel; environment variables are reserved for secrets, bootstrap and deployment topology. Remove ENGAGE_COMMENT_VOTE_RETRY_BUDGET_MS from the vote path. The production budget stays a fixed 5000 ms module constant. Tests pass an explicit optional fifth argument to voteOnComment, an injection point that is validated and clamped to 250-60000 ms; production callers omit it. The expiry warning still records the effective budget. The concurrency tests pass 15000 ms so a loaded runner cannot turn a machine stall into a false failure, and the stuck-writer test passes 1 ms (clamped to the 250 ms floor) so it stays fast. Exactly-once assertions, the persisted shape and the privacy boundary are unchanged. Docs remove the environment-override wording. * chore(changelog): record the injected comment vote retry budget (#123) Regenerates the public snapshot so the refactor appears on /changelog/. * chore(changelog): record bounded comment vote retries after merging main

summary: Remove the tally projection watermark and make rebuilds compare-and-set only (#124)
details: * fix(ballots): make the tally projection rebuild compare-and-set only The merged projection skipped increments whose vote timestamp was at or below an appliedThrough watermark that a rebuild believed it had counted. Under concurrency that watermark was wrong: a vote could be visible to the increment but not the recount, so the increment was skipped and the row under-counted. The full suite failed on main with 7 votes in the row against 8 votes. Remove appliedThrough and its timestamp guard entirely. Increments always apply: each is one atomic upsert of the choice, total and an internal monotonic version. Nothing is skipped. The rebuild is now absolute and compare-and-set only. It reads the row version (0 when the row is missing), recounts every bound vote, and writes absolute counts only if the version is unchanged, advancing it by one. A mismatch recounts and retries, bounded. A concurrent increment either lands before the recount (the absolute write is correct) or after the compare-and-set (it adds on top). The 500 ms deadline still writes nothing, leaving the row for the repair CLI. Revision moves remain transactional deltas and certification still never reads the projection. Tests: 20 rounds that deterministically interleave an increment between the rebuild's recount and its compare-and-set (and after it), asserting exact equality with the authoritative bound tally every round; an increment after an absolute rebuild is applied; the concurrent first-vote, change and revision-move cases remain. The projection test file raises its write deadline under load because a timed-out write is allowed to be abandoned; the timeout case still asserts that nothing is written. Refs #52 * docs(status): record the compare-and-set-only projection rebuild Removes the appliedThrough watermark description and records the merged under-count it caused. Documents the current contract: unconditional atomic increments, transactional revision moves, and an absolute recount that writes only when the row version is unchanged, retries when it moved, and writes nothing at its deadline. Records the 20-round interleaved race test, the 12-test projection suite run ten times, both 713-test full-suite runs, the residual delayed-increment window, and the configurable test deadline. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record the compare-and-set-only tally projection Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record the projection race fix after merging main

summary: Paginate the public list and add a display-only tally projection (#52) (#112)
details: * feat(ballots): project display-only tallies after a committed vote Public list pages (/ and /proposals/) tallied every vote and decrypted every encrypted ballot just to show a count. Add a display-only ballot_tallies row per (ballotId, revisionId), written best-effort after the vote transaction commits. The projection is never authoritative: recordFormalDecision keeps recomputing the outcome from the bound votes and does not read it. A failed or slow projection write is logged as an operational event and cannot fail, delay or alter the vote. Vote changes decrement the previous choice and increment the new one, a re-cast of the same choice is a no-op, and rows are revision-scoped. The row stores counts and a timestamp only: no member id, choice, reason or envelope. listProposals can now omit vote tallies so public reads never touch proposal_votes; the web pages overlay certified results and the projection in the next commit. Adds the unique compound index to initializeDatabase and a rebuild/repair path for the CLI. Refs #52 * perf(proposals): paginate the public list and stop scanning ballots /proposals/ loaded every proposal, applied search, stage, branch and sort in the page, and decrypted every vote for the row totals. It now reads a bounded display page of 25 rows from MongoDB with server-side pagination. - Page, total, page count and range are computed from the filtered set; invalid or out-of-range pages clamp; ties order deterministically by proposal id. - Links keep q, stage, branch, space, sort, focus and joined; changing a filter starts at page 1. Pagination uses the Button primitive with previous/next and a live range status. - Each page self-references its canonical address and emits rel=prev/rel=next. The repository has no noIndex convention for parameterised lists, so pages stay indexable with a self-canonical rather than inventing one. - Rows no longer read proposal_votes. A certified ballot shows the tally stored on ballot_results; otherwise a fresh ballot_tallies row is used; a missing or stale row shows "Voting open — tally updating" with a link to the matter. - / overlays the same projection on the register it already reads, so home no longer decrypts votes either. Matters without a trustworthy aggregate are left out of the highlights rather than showing a wrong percentage. Visibility is still decided by canViewProposal and re-checked after the coarse MongoDB pre-filter; eligibility, ballot binding and deadlines are untouched. Refs #52 * feat(scripts): rebuild the ballot tally projection from votes Add npm run ballots:tally-projection. It reports missing, mismatched and orphan projection rows against the votes they should represent, and with --apply rebuilds them. It never deletes, edits or rewrites a vote and never certifies a result. Dry run is the default; --verify exits non-zero when rows need repair; an explicit --database is required; production writes additionally require --allow-production and --confirm-production engage_production. Encrypted votes need the ballot keys and the tool refuses to write a partial tally without them. Refs #52 * fix(proposals): keep the active stage tab and certified tallies correct The parsed stage is now '' rather than 'all' for an unfiltered list, so the All tab has to compare against '' to stay marked current. A certified result is authoritative even when the matter no longer carries a ballotRevisionId (for example after a zero-vote unbind). Resolve certified results by every visible matter's ballot, not only those with a current binding, so the row shows the recorded tally instead of falling back to no tally. Refs #52 * docs(status): record public list pagination and the tally projection Adds the before/after harness snapshots for / and /proposals/ (before 57402f0, after 65ace21) and records what changed: 25-row server pagination with filter preservation and canonical/rel links, a display-only ballot_tallies projection, certified tallies from ballot_results, and a neutral tally-updating state for missing or stale rows. The profiler window records 3 -> 0 proposal_votes operations on /proposals/ and 6 -> 0 on /, with getMore batches falling from three to one on every measured public page. Reports the /proposals/ HTML increase honestly: it renders 25 rows instead of 15 at the specified page size, not extra markup per row. Updates I12 and S4, notes the detail page's remaining live tally and the deployment step to backfill the projection, and adds the new collection and CLI to the architecture docs. Refs #52 * fix(ballots): move a re-bound amendment tally to the right revision row An amendment ballot can be re-bound to a newer wording revision. A member who had already voted on the previous revision casts again on the new one, so the previous count belongs to the old row, not the new row. The projection now learns the revision the previous vote was bound to and recounts both rows from their votes instead of applying a delta to the wrong row. Main matter ballots cannot reach this path: castVote refuses a ballot whose existing votes are not all bound to its current revision. Adds a projection test for the move. Refs #52 * docs(status): correct the public-list suite count The final run includes the revision-move projection test: 655 tests, 0 fail. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record public list pagination and the tally projection Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. Refs #52 * fix(ballots): make tally projection writes atomic under concurrency The projection's first-vote path read the votes and wrote absolute counts when no row existed. A concurrent increment could land between that read and write, or after it, double counting; the full suite exposed it as an extra abstain. The normal path is now one atomic upsert increment, so a first vote creates the row and counts it in a single operation. Two concurrent first votes can no longer each create a row or lose one. A write conflict from a transactional revision move retries inside the deadline. The only remaining recount is for an unreadable prior vote and the repair CLI. It is compare-and-set guarded on an internal version token and bounded by a watermark recorded in appliedThrough, so an increment for a vote the recount already included is skipped, and an increment that landed first forces a fresh recount. The deadline is enforced before each write (and with maxTimeMS on the recount), so a timed-out rebuild leaves the row for the repair CLI instead of writing a stale absolute count. A revision move is two transactional deltas on the old and new rows, not a recount. A row whose counts are negative or do not sum to its total is never displayed; it reads as tally pending until repaired. Tests: many concurrent first votes, concurrent vote changes and a concurrent revision move each equal the authoritative tally; ten rebuild-versus-increment races; a recorder that a timed-out rebuild writes nothing; and the public list treating an inconsistent row as pending. Refs #52 * docs(status): record the race-safe projection write strategy Replaces the read-then-write description with the atomic strategy: an upsert increment for normal votes, transactional deltas for a revision move, and a compare-and-set recount bounded by a watermark and deadline for the last-resort path. Records that an internally inconsistent row is displayed as pending, the residual out-of-order watermark caveat, the concurrency tests and both full suite results. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record the race-safe tally projection writes Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. summary: Public member profiles and action-led policy changes (#117)
details: * feat(profiles): add public member profiles and editable biography Build a viewer-relative profile read model over existing accounts, comments, proposals, amendments and branch memberships. Profile pages show an initials avatar, optional biography, geographic affiliation, contribution statistics and display-only comment karma, with paginated Comments, Proposals and Amendments tabs and deep links to the exact discussion anchor. Deleted comments, withdrawn amendments and proposals the viewer cannot open are excluded from history, counts and karma. Owners edit a plain-text biography through an origin-checked member route; no separate profile or contribution collection is introduced. Adds profile lookup indexes for comments and amendments. Refs #113 * feat(discussion): link authors to public member profiles Comment names and avatars, the proposal author and amendment authors now link to the public profile when a member id establishes authorship. Disabled accounts render as plain text and truncated historic records without a displayable name are not linked, so the interface never invents an author or offers a dead profile link. Top support and concern takeaways use the same link, and the proposal activity timeline targets the exact amendment anchor. Refs #113 * test(profiles): cover visibility, privacy, pagination and deep links Add in-memory read-model tests for private, branch and archived visibility, deleted comments, withdrawn amendments, legacy policyId comments, karma, deterministic pagination, disabled accounts, historic authors and owner-only biography writes. Add route checks for session and origin enforcement. Add a Chromium harness that follows an author link from a discussion, checks profile tabs and statistics, follows a comment deep link, verifies empty tabs and the 404 page on desktop and mobile, and wire it into CI after the production build. Refs #113 * docs(profiles): document public profiles, visibility and display-only karma Record the profile read model, owner biography field, viewer-relative filtering, profile indexes, biography route, browser harness, capability rows and the remaining privacy limits. Explicitly state that karma never affects eligibility, permissions or proposal authority. Refs #113 * test(profiles): cover the MongoDB karma aggregation Exercise the profile read model against MongoDB so the database-side karma sum is verified, not only the in-memory fallback. The suite skips when VOTING_TEST_MONGODB_URI is not configured and uses a unique database name. Refs #113 * refactor(profiles): rename comment karma to comment score Use the accurate product term for the sum of net scores on visible comments, and remove the always-visible explanatory note. Rename the internal field and function so the old term cannot return through future UI work. Refs #113 * feat(proposals): make policy changes follow the chosen action The policy-change form now treats amend, replace and repeal as distinct member tasks. The selected action drives the page heading, default title, primary question, effect timing and visible fields. Repeal asks for a rationale and hides commitments; an amendment can name the part to change; a replacement can carry proposed wording. Policy changes inherit the published policy's topic and governance context, so members no longer re-enter a topic or scope. Open change proposals for the same policy are shown before the form so members can join the discussion. The action-specific fields are stored with the proposal, included in the revision snapshot and locked once voting begins. Fixes the stale Amend title when Repeal is selected. Refs #114, #97 * test(proposals): guard action-led policy change form wiring Assert that the action selector announces the choice, the page updates the title and question from the chosen action, repeal hides commitments, and the form inherits the policy topic while showing existing change proposals. Refs #114 * chore(changelog): record public profiles and policy change UX Refresh the public snapshot for public member profiles and the action-led policy-change form. Preserve entries outside the generator's 80-commit window so the public history is not shortened. Refs #113, #114

summary: Thread comments with Reddit-style voting and Best ranking (#110)
details: * feat(discussion): render threaded replies with confidence-weighted voting Proposal discussion now stores parentCommentId and depth, renders one recursive comment component instead of a flat list, and keeps replies inside their parent's subtree when sorting. Deleting a comment that still has replies clears the body and keeps a placeholder so the thread does not lose context. Comments take upvotes and downvotes with one active vote per member. Responses return aggregate score, counts and percentage plus the caller's own choice; voter identities are never serialised. The default Best sort applies a Wilson score lower bound to every sibling group, with Top score, Newest and Oldest as alternatives and deterministic tie-breaking. Refs #57. * chore(ci): verify threaded discussion in a real browser Runs the isolated Playwright harness after the perimeter check. It proves parent-first nesting, sibling sorting, deep mobile layout, reply/delete interactions and that the comment API returns aggregate signal only. Refs #57. * docs(discussion): document threading, comment votes and Best ranking Updates the canonical model, API contract, capability matrix and known gaps. Records that comment votes are display ranking only, that voter identities are never returned, and the residual risks around rate limiting, audit and exact aggregate downvote counts. Refs #57. * chore(changelog): record threaded discussion and comment voting Refreshes the public snapshot after the discussion feature, CI verification and documentation commits. The generator's existing 80-commit window still drops older entries (#96); no history was edited by hand. Refs #57. * fix(discussion): make comment vote writes atomic under concurrency Adds a voteVersion compare-and-swap to comment vote updates. A concurrent vote bumps the version, so a stale write is retried against the latest state rather than overwriting it. Covers 25 simultaneous voters and same-member double clicks against both the in-memory database and a real MongoDB replica set. Refs #57. * chore(changelog): record atomic comment vote updates Refs #57. * fix(activity): show the comment's net score, not upvotes alone Member activity previously labelled a contribution with its upvote count, which is misleading now that comments can be downvoted. Show the net score as points, consistent with the discussion thread, and keep vote identities out of the feed. Refs #57. * chore(changelog): record the activity score fix Refs #57. * chore(changelog): regenerate after merging main * fix(discussion): guard tombstoned comments, empty menus, and vote actions

summary: Replace the notification React island with a native disclosure (#52) (#111)
details: * perf(header): replace the notification React island with a native disclosure The signed-in header fetched unread notifications from a React island hydrated with client:idle, which shipped the React runtime (~330 KB) on every signed-in page for one small bell. The bell is now a native <details>/<summary> disclosure backed by a small vanilla module. It reads the same read-only inbox endpoint without caching, only after idle or first open, and renders the latest five notifications. Escape closes it and restores summary focus, outside clicks close it, and only one header panel stays open. Without JavaScript the summary's anchor still opens the notification centre. Marking notifications as read remains in the member notification centre. Refs #52 * fix(header): match the notification panel to the established header shadow * docs(perf): record the React-free header measurements and remaining #52 scope The audit now reports the signed-in header before/after harness snapshots, the pages that no longer ship React, the unchanged database command counts and the inline-script trade-off on anonymous pages. The tracker's I12 line records the header slice as done while leaving the tally read model and member-list pagination as the remaining #52 work. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): refresh the snapshot for the header performance work * fix(header): keep a retry from issuing duplicate inbox reads * chore(changelog): refresh the snapshot for the header retry guard * chore(changelog): record the header performance work after merging main

summary: Keep unread updates and label votes correctly (#108, #56) (#109)
details: * fix(member): keep unread updates until the member dismisses them My Engage advanced engage_member_last_seen on every page load, so navigating away and back hid updates the member never opened. Reading the page now only resolves the window; the cursor advances only through POST /api/member/updates/dismiss. Adds a 'Mark updates as seen' action to the catch-up digest, a matching status message, a seven-day window for members who have never dismissed updates, and a pure helper so the window, list and counts share one rule. Refs #108 * fix(admin): classify votes as votes in the participation feed The panel built vote activities with kind 'vote' but only handled 'votes', so every vote rendered as a proposal submission with the wrong filter and count. Encrypted ballot records carry no member identity, which made the mismatch affect all recent votes. Votes, contributions and proposals now share one classifier and one seven-day window. Vote rows use the recorded timestamp and the existing canViewIdentifiableBallots gate; encrypted records render as 'A member' and choices, reasons, tallies and envelopes are never read. Replayed records collapse by ballot and voter, while separate ballots and voters remain separate rows. The summary strip and tabs are derived from the same rows, and the previously truncated feed now shows the whole window. Refs #56 * chore(changelog): regenerate snapshot for member updates and participation fixes * chore(changelog): record the member and participation fixes
